scope: THE ENTITY LIST LAYOUT, READ FROM 0x671650: two gate bits, a count, then 12 bits per entity id

the_decoder_0x671650.0x671650: memset(0x7859358, 0, 0x1204) - clear the entity id list
the_decoder_0x671650.0x671698: mov [0x7859558], al - THIS IS THE ENTITY COUNT, stored as a BYTE
the_decoder_0x671650.0x6716A1: call 0x66EC30 with push 0xC -> READ 12 BITS per entity id
the_decoder_0x671650.0x6716AD: mov word [ecx*2 + 0x7859358], ax - store the id
the_decoder_0x671650.0x6716BF: cmp bl,al ; jb 0x6716A1 - loop count times

why_the_count_read_as_0xFFFF0000: the count is a BYTE at 0x7859558, and our earlier dword read returned 0xFFFF0000
so the byte is 0x00 and its neighbours are 0xFF, which is exactly what the 0xFF memset at 0x671661 leaves
therefore the count really is ZERO - and the block either took one of the two gate branches, or 0x66ED70 returned 0
the_recipe_to_get_one_entity: then the count must decode to 1 (whatever 0x66ED70 requires)
then 12 bits give the entity id
next: read 0x66ED70 to learn how the count is encoded - it is the only unknown left in this recipe
then build a body with bit1=1, bit2=1, count=1, id=whatever, and check that 0x7859558 reads 1
